questions.question: A 400 m long train is running at the speed of 90 km/hr. Find the time taken by it to pass a man standing near the railway line.
questions.explanation:
Speed of train= 90 kmph = 518×90 = 25 m/s

length of trains \(= \ 400\ m\)

Time taken by train to pass the man \(= \frac{400}{25}\ \  = 16\ sec\)

questions.question: A 200 m long train is running at the speed of 72 km/hr. Find the time taken by it to pass a man standing near the railway line.
questions.explanation:
Length of train\(\  = \ 200\ m\)

Speed of train = 72 kmph =\(\ 72 \times \frac{5}{18}\  = \ 20\ m/s\)

Time taken to cross the man \(= \ \frac{200}{20}\  = \ 10\ sec\)

questions.question: A man is moving with a speed of 20 km/hr. After every km, he takes a rest of 3 minutes. How much time will he take to cover a distance of 75 km?
questions.explanation:
Given Information:
• Speed = 20 km/hr
• Distance = 75 km
• Rest after every 1 km = 3 minutes

Calculation:
Time to travel 75 km without rest
= 75 ÷ 20 hours
= 3.75 hours
= 3 hours 45 minutes

Number of rests
= 75 − 1 = 74

Total rest time
= 74 × 3 = 222 minutes
= 3 hours 42 minutes

Total time
= 3 hours 45 minutes + 3 hours 42 minutes
= 7 hours 27 minutes

Alternate Method:
For every 1 km
Travel time = 60 ÷ 20 = 3 minutes

So each km takes 3 + 3 = 6 minutes (including rest)

For 75 km
= 75 × 6 = 450 minutes

But last km has no rest
So subtract 3 minutes

Total = 447 minutes
= 7 hours 27 minutes

Final Answer: 7 hours 27 minutes
Hence, option C is correct.

Used Concepts:
• Time = Distance ÷ Speed
• Counting number of breaks
• Conversion of hours to minutes

questions.question: There are two points A and B. Distance between A and B is \(245\ km\). Ram starts walking from A with a speed of \(15\ km\ /\ h\) and lakhan starts from B with a speed of \(20\ km\ /\ h\). Find the time when both meet.
questions.explanation:
Relative speed = (20 + 15) km / h    (if opposite direction)

= 35 km / h

∴ Required time = 245 / 35 = 7 hours

questions.question: A car travelling at a speed of 80 km/hour can complete a journey in 5 hours. How long will it take to travel the same distance at 50 km/hour?
questions.explanation:
Total distance travelled by car \(= \ 80 \times 5\  = \ 400\ km\)

Time taken by car while traveling at 50 km/ hr\(\  = \ \frac{400}{50} = \ 8\ hr\)

questions.question: A can cover a distance from P to Q in 5 hours and the distance between P and Q is 200 km. If B can cover the same distance but he goes from Q towards P and they meet after 2 hours of start, then find the speed of B.
questions.explanation:
Let the speed of B be x kmph.

Distance between P and Q \(= \ 200km.\)

Speed of A \(= \ \frac{200}{5} = \ 40\ kmph\)

Relative speed of A and B\(\  = 40 + x\ \ kmph\)

Time taken to meet\(\  = \ 2\ hours\)

200x+40 =2

\( 2x\  = \ 120\)

\( x\  = \ 60\ kmph\)

questions.question: A can cover a distance from P to Q in 10 hours and the distance between P and Q is 300 km. If B can cover the same distance but he goes from Q towards P and they meet after 5 hours of start, then find the speed of B.
questions.explanation:
Let speed of B be k km/hr

Relative speed \(= \ k + 30\ km/hr\)

Distance between P and Q \(= \ 300\ km\)

Speed of A\(\  = \ \frac{300}{10} = \ 30\ km/hr\)

Time taken to meet = 5 hr

\( \frac{300}{k + 30} = 5\)

\( k + 30 = 60\)

\( k = 30\ km/hr\ \)

∴ Hence the answer is 30 km/hr

Time taken to cross the faster train =\(\ \frac{500}{25} = 20\ sec\)

questions.question: A and B are traveling towards each other from the points P and Q respectively. After crossing each other, A and B take 4 and 9 hours respectively to reach their destination Q and P respectively. If the speed of B is 18 kmph, then find the speed of A.
questions.explanation:

 Speed of Car A = x kmph

questions.question: A boy goes to his school from his house at a speed of 10 km/hr and returns at a speed of 5 km/hr. If he takes 6 hours in going and coming, find the distance between his house and school.
questions.explanation:
Let the total distance between house and school be k km.

As per question;

\(\frac{k}{10} + \frac{k}{5} = 6\)

\( \frac{15k}{50} = 6\)

\( k\  = \ 20\ km\)

questions.question: A and B are traveling towards each other from the points P and Q respectively. After crossing each other, A and B take 16 and 9 hours respectively to reach their destination Q and P respectively. Speed of A SA= x kmph

SBSA=TATB

8x=169

x = 6 kmph

questions.question: A Truck can go 100 km in 5 hours but there was an accident midway. After the accident, the speed of the truck reduces by 25%. If the accident occurs after covering 40 km, then find the total time taken by Truck.
questions.explanation:
Speed of truck\(= \ \frac{100}{5}\  = 20\ km/hr\)

Speed of truck after accident \(= \frac{3}{4} \times 20 = 15\ km/hr\)

Remaining distance after accident\(\  = \ 100 - 40 = \ 60\ km\)

Time taken by Truck  \(= \ \frac{40}{20} + \frac{60}{15} = \ 6\ hr\)

questions.question: Two trucks ‘A’ and ‘C’ were moving towards each other which were 540 km away initially. If the ratio of the speed of the trucks ‘A’ and ‘C’ was 5 : 4 and the speed of the truck ‘C’ was 60 km/h, what time will it take for the two trucks to meet each other?
questions.explanation:
Given Information:
• Initial distance between trucks A and C = 540 km
• Ratio of speed of truck A to truck C = 5 : 4
• Speed of truck C = 60 km/h

Calculation:
Speed of truck A = (5 / 4) * Speed of truck C
Speed of truck A = (5 / 4) * 60 = 75 km/h
Since both trucks are moving towards each other, relative speed = Speed of truck A + Speed of truck C
Relative speed = 75 + 60 = 135 km/h
Time taken to meet = Initial Distance / Relative Speed
Time taken to meet = 540 / 135 = 4 hours
Time in minutes = 4 * 60 = 240 minutes

Hence, option (B) is correct.

Used Concepts:
• Relative Speed (Opposite Direction)
• Time, Speed, and Distance Relationship

questions.question: In a 1500 m race, Chetna beats Vrutika by 100 m and in 1200 m race, Vrutika beats Kripa by 75 m. If Chetna and Kripa are compared, then for how much m Chetna will beat Kripa in 900 m race?
questions.explanation:
From the given information,

Chetna can beat Vrutika by 100 m in 1500 m race.

Hence, when Chetna covers 1500 m, Vrutika covers 1400 m.

So when Chetna covers 900 m, Vrutika will cover 840 m.

Similarly, when Vrutika covers 1200 m, Kripa covers 1125 m.

So, when Vrutika covers 840 m, Kripa will cover 787.5 m.

∴ Chetna will beat Kripa by 112.5 m.

questions.question: Krishna covered a distance of 400 km in 10 hrs. The first part of his journey is covered by train, then he hired a taxi. The speed of the train and taxi is 30 km/hr and 45 km /hr respectively. Find the ratio of distance covered by train and taxi.
questions.explanation:
Given Information:

  • Total distance = 400 km

  • Total time = 10 hours

  • Speed of train = 30 km/hr

  • Speed of taxi = 45 km/hr

Used Concept:

  • Distance = Speed × Time

  • Let time in train = x, then time in taxi = (10 − x)

Solution:
Distance covered by train = 30x
Distance covered by taxi = 45(10 − x)

According to the question:
30x + 45(10 − x) = 400
30x + 450 − 45x = 400
−15x = −50
x = 10/3

Distance by train = 30 × (10/3) = 100 km
Distance by taxi = 400 − 100 = 300 km

Required ratio = 100 : 300 = 1 : 3

So, the answer is 1 : 3.

questions.question: A car is proceeding towards A at a uniform speed of 30 km/hr. While the car is 150 kms away from A an insect starting from A flies again and again between A and the car relentlessly. The speed of the insect is 40km/hr. Find the distance covered by the insect till the car reaches A.
questions.explanation:
Time taken by car to reach A when its is 150 kms aways = \(\frac{150}{30}\  = \ 5\ hrs\)

Speed of insect = 40 kmph

Distance travelled by insect in 5 hrs \(= \ 40 \times 5\  = \ 200\ km\)

questions.question: A car going from A to B and again returning from B to A and in this journey the total time taken is 35 hours. If the distance between A and B is 210 km, then find the average speed of the car in this whole journey.
questions.explanation:
Average Speed \(= \frac{\text{Total Distance }}{\text{Time taken}}\)

\(= \ \frac{210 + 210}{35} = 12\ km/hr\)

questions.question: A car going from A to B and again returning from B to A and in this journey the total time taken is 48 hours. If the distance between A and B is 720 km, then find the average speed of the car in this whole journey.
questions.explanation:
Distance between A and B = 720 km

Average Speed \(= \frac{\text{Total Distance travelled between A and B }}{\text{ Total Time taken}}\)

\(= \frac{720 + \ 720}{48} = 30\ km/hr\)

questions.question: Ananya drives the first 180 miles of her trip at a speed of 80 km/hr and the rest of the trip at 110 km/hr. Her average speed for the entire trip is 100 km/hr. Find the length of the trip. (1 mile ~ 1.6 km)
questions.explanation:
Given Information:
• First part of distance = 180 miles
• Speed for the first part = 80 km/hr
• Speed for the remaining part = 110 km/hr
• Average speed for the entire trip = 100 km/hr
• Conversion: 1 mile ≈ 1.6 km

Calculation:
Let the total length of the trip be 'x' miles.
Total distance in km = 1.6x
Time taken for the first part = (180 × 1.6) / 80 hours
Time taken for the remaining part = [(x - 180) × 1.6] / 110 hours
We know, Average Speed = Total Distance / Total Time
100 = (1.6x) / [ (180 × 1.6) / 80 + ((x - 180) × 1.6) / 110 ]
Dividing both numerator and denominator of the right side by 1.6:
100 = x / [ 180 / 80 + (x - 180) / 110 ]
100 = x / [ 2.25 + (x - 180) / 110 ]
x = 100 × [ 2.25 + (x - 180) / 110 ]
x = 225 + [ 10 × (x - 180) / 11 ]
11x = 2475 + 10x - 1800
11x - 10x = 675
x = 675 miles

Alternate Method:
Using Weighted Average of Times:
Let T1 and T2 be times for the two parts.
Average Speed = (S1 × T1 + S2 × T2) / (T1 + T2)
100 = (80 × T1 + 110 × T2) / (T1 + T2)
100T1 + 100T2 = 80T1 + 110T2
20T1 = 10T2
T2 / T1 = 2 / 1
Time for first part (T1) = (180 × 1.6) / 80 = 3.6 hours
Since T2 = 2 × T1, T2 = 7.2 hours
Distance of second part in km = 7.2 × 110 = 792 km
Distance of second part in miles = 792 / 1.6 = 495 miles
Total distance = 180 + 495 = 675 miles

Used Concepts:
• Time = Distance / Speed
• Average Speed = Total Distance / Total Time

Exam Insight:
In average speed problems involving unit conversions, if the conversion factor applies to all distance or speed terms uniformly, it often cancels out. Focus on the ratios to save time.

questions.question: A fired a bullet and after (x+3) sec it was heard by B who was standing at a certain distance from the place where the bullet fired. If the speed of air is x m/sec and the distance between A and B is 10 meters, then find the value of x.
questions.explanation:
Distance = 10m

Time \(= \ (x + 3)\ sec\)

Speed of air = x m/sec

ATP

\(\frac{10}{x} = (x + 3)\)

=> \(x^{2} + 3x - 10 = 0\)

=> \(x^{2} + 5x - 2x - 10 = 0\)

=> \({x(x + 5) - 2(x + 5) = 0}^{}\)

=> \((x - 2)(x + 5) = 0\)

=> \(x = + 2,\  - 5\)

Value of x cannot be in negative

so the value of x = 2

questions.question: A bus left town A for town B. Having traveled 33.33% of the distance, it stopped for 5 hours due to road blockage. It traveled 300 km of the total distance by this time. After it started again, the driver increased the speed by 25 km/h and reached town B at the scheduled time. What was the original speed of the bus?
questions.explanation:
Let the original speed of the bus be x kmph.

Total distance to travel\(\  = \ 3 \times 300\  = \ 900\ km\)

Remaining distance\(\  = \ 900 - 300 = \ 600\ km\)

New speed\(\  = \ x + 25\ kmph\)

As per question;

Time taken to travel 300 km will be equal to 5 hours more than time taken to travel the rest 600 km

\(\frac{300}{x} = \frac{600}{x + 25} + 5\)

\( (\frac{300}{x}) - (\frac{600}{x + 25}) = 5\)

\( \ x\  = \ 15\)

The original speed of the bus is 15 kmph

questions.question: A gun fired 2 bullets in an interval of 20 minutes at a place but a person running towards the place heard it after 18 minutes from the first firing. If the speed of the sound in 234 m/s, then find the speed of the person.
questions.explanation:
Let the speed of the person be ‘x’

Total distance covered by the sound of 1st bullet - Total distance covered by sound of 2nd bullet = Total distance covered by the person

\(= > (234 \times 20\  - 234 \times 18)60 = x \times \ 18\  \times 60\ \)

\(= > x = speed\ of\ the\ person\  = \ 26\ m/s\ \)

questions.question: A gun fired in an interval of 10 minutes at a place but a person running towards the place heard it after 8 minutes from the first firing. If the speed of the sound is 320 m/s, then find the speed of the person.
questions.explanation:
Let the speed of the person be x m/s.

Time delay is listening the gun sound\(\  = \ 10 - 8\  = \ 2\ min\)

Distance travelled by bullet in 2 min \(= \ 2\  \times 320\ m\)

As per question;

\(2 \times 320 = \ 8 \times x\)

\(= > x\  = \ 80\ m/s\)

questions.question: A gun fired in an interval of 25 minutes at a place but a person running towards the place heard it after 20 minutes from the first firing. If the speed of the sound is 300 m/s, then find the speed of the person in kmph.
questions.explanation:
Let the speed of the person be x m/s.

Time delay in listening the gun fired \(= \ 25 - 20\  = \ 5\ \ min\  = \ 300\ sec\)

Distance travelled by bullet in 300 sec \(= \ 300 \times 300\ m\)

As per question;

\(300 \times 300 = x \times 20 \times 60\)

\(= > x = \ 75\ m/s\  = \ 75 \times \frac{18}{5}\  = \ 270\ kmph\)

questions.question: A gun fired two shots at an interval and the person who was coming on the bike heard it after 10 minutes. If the speed of the bike was 180 kmph and the speed of sound is 300 m/sec, then find the actual interval of the shots fired.
questions.explanation:
Let the actual interval of the shot fired be k sec.

Total distance covered by the sound of 1st bullet - Total distance covered by sound of 2nd bullet = Total distance covered by the bike

\(= > (300 \times k\  - 300 \times 10)60 = Speed\ of\ bike\ \  \times \ 12\  \times 60\)

\(= > 300(k - 10) = 180 \times (\frac{5}{18}) \times 12\)

\(= > k - 10 = 2\)

\(= > k\  = \ 12\ sec\ \)

questions.question: A person starts from a point and walks at the speed of 30km/h  for 30minutes and then he gets the lift from a person on bike and then he travels at a speed of60  km/hr for the next 30 minutes. What is the total distance moved by the person from the starting point?
questions.explanation:
We know that speed=distance travelled/time

30 minutes = 30/60 =1/2 hours

Let us take the first case when he was walking

total distance=(speed of walking)(time taken)

30(1/2)=15km……………………………..(1)

Now he got the lift and new speed=60km/h

For next 30 minutes distance traveled=(speed)(time taken)

60(1/2)=30km…………………………….(2)

Adding equations 1 and 2 we get the total distance:

So total distance moved=15+30=45km

questions.question: 'A' and 'B' start running together from point 'X' towards point 'Y'. At the same time, 'C' leaves from point 'Y' towards point 'X'. 'C' meets 'A' and 'B' at points 'M' and 'N' respectively, which are 150 metre and 75 metres away from point 'X'. Find the ratio of speed of 'A' to 'B', given that 'X' and 'Y' are 225 metres apart.
questions.explanation:
Given, 'C' meets 'A' and 'B' at points 'M' and 'N' respectively, which are 150 metre and 75 metres away from point 'X'

XN = 75 metres

XM = 150 metres

Therefore, NM = 150 - 75 = 75 metres

Therefore, XN = XM = 75 metres

Also, YM = 225 - 75 - 75 = 75 metres

Distance covered by 'A' by the time he meets 'C' = 150 metres

Distance covered by 'C' during the same duration = 75 metres

Since time taken by 'A' and 'C' is same, the ratio of speeds of 'A' and 'C' will be same as the ratio of distance covered by them.

So, ratio of speeds of 'A' and 'C' = 150:75 = 2:1

Similarly, distance covered by 'B' by the time he meets 'C' = 75 metres

Distance covered by 'C' during the same duration = 150 metres

So, ratio of speeds of 'B' and 'C' = 75:150 = 1:2

Let the speed of 'A' be 2x m/s

So, speed of 'C' = (2x/2) = x m/s

And speed of 'B' = (x/2) = (x/2) m/s

So, required ratio = 2x:(x/2) = 4:1

Hence, option a.

questions.question: A cyclist, after cycling a distance of 50 km on the first day, finds that the ratio of distance covered by him on the first two days is 5:4. If he travels a distance of 60 km on the third day. If the speed of the cyclist is 5 kmph, then find the time taken to cover the distance equal to the difference of distance on the third day and first day.
questions.explanation:
Distance covered in 1st : 2nd day \(= \ 5:4\)

\( 50:\ 2nd\ day\  = \ 5:4\)

 Distance covered in 2nd day\(\  = \ 40\ km\ \)

Difference of 1st day and 3rd distance\(\  = \ 60 - 50\  = \ 10\ km\)

Time taken to cover 10 km \(= \ \frac{10}{5} = \ 2\ hr\)

questions.question:
Directions: Study the following question carefully and choose the right answer given beside.

Amardeep goes to park daily. His last week average speed with which he completed one round of the park was 47Km/h, for the first four days was 37Km/h, and that for the last four days was 52.5Km/h. Find out the time taken by Amardeep to travel 203 Km if he travels with the speed of the fourth day.
questions.explanation:
From the given information,

Let, Speed on the fourth day = a

total speed for the first three days = X

& total speed for the last three days = Y

Now,

Total speed for the week, S = 47 × 7 = 329

Total speed for the first four days = X + a = 37 × 4 = 148

Total speed for the last four days = Y + a = 52.5 × 4 = 210

According to the question,

X + a + Y = S

⇒ (X + a) + (Y + a) – a = 329

⇒ 148 + 210 – a = 329

⇒ a = 358 – 329

⇒ a = 29 Km/h

Therefore, time taken to travel 203 km \(= \frac{203}{29} = 7\ hours\)

questions.question: A constable follows a thief who is 250 m ahead of the constable. If the constable and the thief run at speeds of 54 km/hour and 18 km/hour respectively, would the constable catch the thief in what time?
questions.explanation:
Given:
Distance between constable and thief = 250 m
Speed of constable = 54 km/h
Speed of thief = 18 km/h

Calculation:

Relative speed of constable and thief \(= \ 54 - 18 = \ 36\ kmph\  = \ 10\ m/s\)

Distance between them \(= \ 250\ m\)

Time taken to catch the thief \(= \ \frac{250}{10}\  = \ 25\ sec\)

Concept used:
Time = Distance ÷ (Relative speed)

questions.question: A car travels from P to Q at a constant speed. If its speed were increased by 5 km/h, it would have taken one hour less to cover the distance. It would have taken 4 hours less if the speed was further increased by 40 km/h. If the speed initially was 45 kmph, then find the distance between the two cities and time taken in the last assumption in which speed increased by 40 kmph..
questions.explanation:
According to question:

Case 1. speed were increased by 5 km/h, and by this it takes 1 hour less to cover distance

Case 2. if the speed was further increased by 40 km/h, then it takes 4 hours less

The Initital speed of Car = 45 kmph

Distance between two cities and time of last Case = ?

Let the distance to reach his office be x km.

As per question;

\(\frac{x}{45} + \frac{x}{50} = 1\)

\( 50\ x - 45\ x = 45 \times 50\)

\( 5x = 45 \times 50\)

\( x\  = \ 450\ km\)

So, final speed\(\  = 45 + 5 + 40\  = \ 90\ kmph\)

Time taken \(= \ \frac{450}{90} = \ 5\ hr\)

 

Other Solution:

 

Constant Product Ratio (CPR): By this method we can solve this question in seconds.

Think Without Ink: Speed always depends on time, and time depends on speed. As the speed increases, the time keeps decreasing. In the question, the initial speed is 45, and when the speed increases by 5, the ratio will be 5/45, or we can also say that speed increases by 1/9. so the time will decrease by 1/10  (in question it is given that time decrease by 1 hour at first)

so 1 unit = 1 hour

10 unit = 10 hour (it will be initial time when car travels 45km/hr)

so distance = Time ×  Speed

Distance = 10 × 45 = 450 km

This is only in option D, that’s why the correct answer will be option D, by this no need to solve further question

 How does CPR work:

        xy→ xx+y

19→11+9      ⇒  110

 


Note: CPR can be used in such questions where one thing depends on the other, and the other thing depends on the first one.

questions.question: A car driver leaves Bangalore at 9.30 A.M. and expects to reach a place 300 km from Bangalore at 1.30 P.M. At 11.30 he finds that he has covered only 30% of the distance. By how much does he has to increase the speed of the car in order to keep up his schedule?
questions.explanation:
Distance covered till 11:30 a.m\(.\  = \ 30\%\ of\ 300\  = \ 90\ km\)

Speed of the car till 11: 30 a.m \(= \ \frac{90}{2} = \ 45\ km/hr\)

Remaining distance\(\  = \ 300 - 90\  = \ 210\ km\)

Speed of car to reach Bangalore at time\(= \ \frac{210}{2} = \ 105\ km/hr\)

Therefore; speed should increase by \((105 - 45) = \ 60\ km/hr\)

questions.question: Distance between two bus stations X and Y is 500 km. Buses P and Q leave station X and Y at 9 a.m. and 11 a.m. respectively at the speed of 50 kmph and 30 kmph respectively for the journey towards Y and X respectively. If the time taken by Q to meet bus P is k hrs. Then find = 50% of k + 150% of k
questions.explanation:
Relative speed of buses \(= \ 50 + 30 = \ 80\ kmph\)

Distance travelled by P till 11 am \(= \ 50 \times 2 = \ 100\ km\)

Remaining distance\(\  = \ 500 - 100\  = \ 400\ km\)

Time taken by Q to meet P ,k\(= \ \ \frac{400}{80} = \ 5\ hrs\)

Therefore; 50% of k + 150% of k =\(\ 2.5 + 7.5\  = \ 10\ \)

questions.question: 45 pillars are standing in a line such that distance between any two consecutive pillars is the same. A car traveling with a uniform speed of 72 km/h takes 18 sec to reach the 1st pole to the 10th pole. What is the distance between the 10th and 31st poles?
questions.explanation:
Let the distance between the 1st pole and 10th pole will be 9 units.

So, Time is taken to cross 1 unit \(= \frac{18}{9} \Rightarrow 2\) seconds

Given, a uniform speed of the car \(= 72\ km/h\)

Speed \(= 72 \times \frac{5}{18} \Rightarrow 20\ m/s\)

So, the distance between two poles \(= 1\) unit

As we know,

\(speed = \frac{\text{distance }}{\text{time}}\)

So, distance \(= 20 \times 2 \Rightarrow 40\ m\)

Hence, the distance between the 10th to 31st pole will be \(31 - 10 \Rightarrow 21\) units

\(21 \times 40\ m \Rightarrow 840\ m\)

questions.question: A bus leaves a city P at 8:00 A.M. On its way to city Q, it overtakes a motorcycle at 10:00 A.M. and reaches Q at 11:30 A.M. It halts at Q for half an hour and starts moving towards P. It meets the same motorcycle at 1:00 P.M. What is the ratio of the speed of the bus to the speed of the motorcycle?
questions.explanation: As the bus takes 0.5 hrs to travel from R to S and the motorcycle takes 3 hours to travel from R to S. So the ratio of time taken becomes 1:6 and so the speeds are in the ratio of 6:1.

questions.question:
A car covers ____ km in 9 hours. The speed of the train is double of the speed of the car. The train covers 360 km in _____ hours.

Find which of the given options fill the blank to make the statement correct?
questions.explanation:
Let's check the option D,

The speed of the car is \(\frac{540}{9}\) = 60 km/hr.

The speed of the train is 120 km/hr

360 km covers by train in \(\frac{360}{120}\) = 3 hours.

So, it is satisfied.

questions.question: A dog pursues a cat and takes 8 leaps for every 10 leaps of the cat, but 5 leaps of the dog are equal to 3 leaps of the cat. What is ratio of the speeds of the dog and the cat?
questions.explanation:
Let in 5 leaps dog covers d unit and in 3 leaps cat covers d units.

Distance covered by the dog in 1 leap =d5 units and distance covered by the cat in 1 leap =d3 units.

And, in t second dog covers 8 leaps and the cat covers 10 leaps.

Distance covered by the dog in 8 leaps =  8d5units and distance covered by the cat in 10 leaps = 10d3 units.

Speed of dog =8d5t and speed of cat = 10d3t

Required ratio  =8d5t:10d3t= 12: 25

questions.question: The distance between Delhi and Patna is Y km. Train P leaves from Delhi to Patna at a speed of x km/h and at the same time, Train Q leaves from Patna to Delhi at a speed of (x + 9) km/h. At the end of 12 hours, they meet each other and then find the speed of the train Q? Where Y=1260÷6×3-42
questions.explanation:
Y=1260÷6×3-42

Y =210×3-42

Y =630 - 42

Y= 588

The relative speed of train P and Q = x + x + 9 = 2x + 9 km/h
We know,

Distance = Speed × Time
588 = (2x + 9) × 12

2x+9 = 58812

2x+9=49

2x=40

x=20

Speed of the train Q = 20 + 9 = 29 km/h

questions.question: Varun was traveling at the speed of 65 km/h. A car with speed 80 km/h passed Varun and then Varun increased his speed by 5 km/h every hour. When Varun passed the car, he stopped increasing his speed and continued at the current  speed. After passing the car, what was the distance between Varun and the car, after 2 hours?
questions.explanation:
Let, the time taken by Varun to pass the car = x hours

So, distance traveled by the car in x hours = 80x km

Therefore, x22×65+x-1×5=80x

⇒ 12[130 + 5x – 5] = 80

⇒1252+5x2=80 

⇒ 125 + 5x = 160

⇒ 5x = 35

⇒ x = 7

So, after 7 hours, Varun would have passed the car.

The speed of Varun when he passed the car = 65 + (7 – 1) × 5 = 65 + 30 = 95 km/h

Required distance = (95 – 80) × 2 = 15 × 2 = 30 km

Hence, option B is answer.

questions.question: Ranjeet drove from home to his office at 75 miles per hour and reached the office in 6 hours. While returning home he drove one-third way along the same route at a speed of 30 miles per hour and the remaining distance he covered in 2 hours. Find the average speed of returning.
questions.explanation:
Given Information:

  • Speed while going = 75 miles/hour
  • Time taken = 6 hours
  • Return journey:
    • First 1/3 distance at 30 mph
    • Remaining distance in 2 hours

Used Concept:

  • Distance = Speed × Time
  • Average speed = Total distance / Total time

Distance between home and office:
= 75 × 6 = 450 miles

Return journey:

First part distance = 1/3 of 450 = 150 miles
Time taken = 150 / 30 = 5 hours

Remaining distance = 450 − 150 = 300 miles
Time taken = 2 hours

Total return time = 5 + 2 = 7 hours

Average speed = Total distance / Total time
= 450 / 7
= 64.285 miles/hour

So, the average speed during return journey is 64.285 miles/hour.

questions.question: Aman, Beena and Chetan start running around a circular field having circumference 180 metre at the same time from the same point. Speeds of Aman, Beena and Chetan are 2 m/minute, 2.5 m/minute and 3 m/minute. Find after how much time, they will meet again at the same point for the first time.
questions.explanation:
Given:

Time taken by Aman to complete one round of the circular field,

\(= \frac{180}{2} = 90\ minutues\)

Time taken by Beena to complete one round of the circular field,

\(= \frac{180}{2.5} = 72\ minutues\)

Time taken by Chetan to complete one round of the circular field,

\(= \frac{180}{3} = 60\ minutues\)

L.C.M of 90, 72, 60=360 minutes=\(\frac{360}{60} = 6\ hours\)

questions.question: A car can cover a distance of 700 Km in 10 hours. Speed of a bus is 14.28% less than the speed of the car and the speed of a train is 16.66% more than the speed of the bus. Find the respective ratio of the distance covered by the car in 20 hours and distance covered by the train in 10 hours.
questions.explanation:
Speed of car\(\  = \ \frac{700}{10}\  = \ 70\ kmph\)

Speed of bus \(= \ (\frac{6}{7})70\  = \ 60\ kmph\)

Speed of train =\(\ (\frac{7}{6})60\  = \ 70\ kmph\)

Required ratio\(\  = \ (20 \times 70):(70 \times 10) = \ 2:1\ \)

questions.question: A can cover a distance from P to Q in 5.4 hours and the distance between P and Q is (5x+20) km. If B can cover the same distance but he goes from Q towards P and they meet after 3 hours of start, and the speed of A and B is x kmph and  (x-10) kmph, respectively, then find the value of x.
questions.explanation:
Speed of B \(= \ x - 10\ kmph.\)

Distance between P and Q \(= \ 5x + 20\ km.\)

Speed of A = x kmph

Relative speed of A and B \(= \ x + x - 10 = 2x - 10\ kmph\)

Time taken by B to meet A = 3 hours

\( \frac{(5x + 20)}{2x - 10} = 3\)

\( 6x - 30 = 5x + 20\)

\( x = 50\)

questions.question: A can cover a distance from P to Q with the speed of x km/hr and the distance between P and Q is (x+120) km. If B can cover the same distance but he goes from Q towards P and they meet after 2 hours of start and the speed of B is (x-60) kmph, then find the value of x.
questions.explanation:
Speed of A\(\  = x\ km/hr\)

Speed of car B \(= \ (x - 60)\ km/hr\)

Distance between P and Q\(\  = \ x + 120\ km\)

Time taken by car B to meet car A = 2 hr

\( \frac{(x + 120)}{x + x - 60} = 2\)

\( (x + 120) = 2\lbrack 2x - 60\rbrack\)

\( x^{} + 120 = 4x - 120\)

\( x = 80\)

∴ Hence the answer is 80.

questions.question:
Length of train A is X meters that crosses a 250 meters platform in 45 seconds. Length of train B is 500 meters that crosses a bridge in 65/3 seconds and length of the platform is 100 meters more than that of bridge. Speed of train B is 10 m/sec more than train A.

Speed of a boat in still water is 25% speed of train A. If boat covers \(\frac{3X}{5}\) km upstream in 30 hours, then find the speed of current.
questions.explanation:
Let speed of train A be ‘Y’ m/sec.

And speed of train B be ‘Y+10’ m/sec.

According to question,

\(\frac{X\  + \ 250}{Y}\) = 45………..(i)

And

\(\frac{500\  + \ 150}{Y\  + \ 10\ }\) = \(\frac{65}{3}\)

30 – 10 = Y

Y = 20

Putting value of Y in (i)

\(\frac{X\  + \ 250}{20}\) = 45

900 – 250 = X

X = 650

Boat cover total distance = 3 \(\times\) \(\frac{650}{5}\) = 390 km

Speed of boat in still water = 20 \(\times \frac{18}{5} \times \frac{25}{100}\) = 18 km/hr

Let speed of current be V km/hr

According to question,

\(\frac{390}{18 - V}\) = 30

13 = 18 – V

V = 5 km/hr

questions.question:
Direction: Study the following data carefully and answer the questions:

Bus P started running at 12:30 PM from point A to point B and bus Q started running at 2:30 PM from point A to point B. Time taken by bus P to reach point B is 2.5 hours more than that taken by bus Q to reach point B. Ratio of speed of bus P to that of bus Q is 3:4 and distance between points A and B is 648 km.

Which of the following is/are true?

M: If speed of bus P were 15% less than its original speed, then it would not reach point B on the same day.

N: Speed of bus P is 8 m/s less than that of bus Q.

O: Bus Q will reach point B at 9:00 PM.
questions.explanation:
Let speeds of bus P and bus Q are ‘3x’ km/h and ‘4x’ km/h respectively.

Since, time taken by bus P to reach point B is 2.5 hours more than that taken by bus Q to reach point B.

So,

\(\left( \frac{648}{3x} \right)\ –\ \left( \frac{648}{4x} \right)\) = 2.5

\(\left( \frac{216}{x} \right)–\ \left( \frac{162}{x} \right)\) = 2.5

\(\frac{54}{x}\) = 2.5

x = 21.6

Speed of bus P = 3 × 21.6 = 64.8 km/h

Speed of bus Q = 4 × 21.6 = 86.4 km/h

Time taken by bus P to reach point B = \(\frac{648}{64.8}\) = 10 hours

Time taken by bus Q to reach point B = \(\frac{648}{86.4}\) = 7.5 hours

From M,

If speed of bus P were 15% less than its original speed.

So, new speed of bus P would be = 85% of 64.8 = 55.08 km/h

And time taken by bus P to reach point B would be = \(\frac{648}{55.08}\) = 11.76 hours (approximately) = 11 hours 46 minutes (approximately)

The time, at which bus P will reach point B = 12:16 AM (on next day)

So, M is true.

From N,

Speed of bus P = 3 × 21.6 = 64.8 km/h

Speed of bus Q = 4 × 21.6 = 86.4 km/h

Required difference = (86.4 – 64.8) × \(\left( \frac{5}{18} \right)\) = 6 m/s

So, N is not true.

From O,

Time taken by bus Q to reach point B = 7.5 hours = 7 hours 30 minutes

So, the time, at which bus Q will reach point B = 10:00 PM

So, O is not true.

Hence, only M is true.
